Entity Description / Overview:
SustainGenix GmbH (Lörrach, Germany) is a space-downstream software, social impact, and geo-information enterprise specialising in high-altitude climate resilience, spatial risk analytics, and off-grid hazard intelligence. The company owns and governs the intellectual property of the 1,700 km Great Himalaya Trail (GHT) spatial dataset, built upon fifteen years of georeferenced field exploration, high-altitude mapping, and extensive research on tourism impacts across fragile mountain ecosystems.
SustainGenix develops the "Human-Digital Twin" Safety Engine, a 3-tier technology architecture bridging space-borne sensors with community-based observation and research, and storytelling:

Space Layer: Ingestion and automated processing of European Space Agency (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data for cloud-penetrating interferometry (InSAR), surface deformation tracking, and Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) monitoring across complex mountain terrain.

AI & Cloud Layer: Dialect-adapting, offline-first speech-to-text AI models (Sherpa, Tamang, Nepali) and serverless cloud analytics that convert spoken local reports into structured, georeferenced spatial vectors and real-time B2B enterprise risk APIs.

Ground-Truth & Community Layer: Deployment of ruggedised satellite communicators and mobile tools to local micro-entrepreneurs (female teahouse hosts) and licensed trekking guides. This layer functions both as an off-grid safety network and as a digital platform for community storytelling, preserving cultural heritage and publishing local narratives in native dialects.

Research & Commercial Capabilities: SustainGenix conducts field research into mountain tourism impacts, socio-economic equity, and climate adaptation. The company actively promotes responsible tourism along Himalayan corridors by supporting firewood elimination, waste management, and direct economic inclusion. SustainGenix commercialises its spatial assets through enterprise hazard APIs for tour operators and travel insurers (Duty of Care compliance), B2C dynamic safety navigation apps (FarOut, OutdoorActive and ride with GPS, B2G/NGO cryosphere change analytics, and white-label "Dynamic Trail OS" software licensing for international mountain trail authorities worldwide.

NEMA Systems Ltd combines advanced electrical and electro-mechanical design capability, decades of aerospace, defence and space actuation and certification experience and established UK manufacturing capability to develop and industrialise high-performance motors, power electronics, drives and actuation systems. Our integrated approach brings together engineering, manufacturing and test capability to reduce development risk, accelerate programmes and provide customers with a single, experienced partner for demanding applications.
Quality and traceability are embedded throughout our approach. Decades of experience through our parent company NEMA Ltd allows us to design and manufacture to AS9100 Rev D, alongside ISO 9001 and relevant OEM supplier approvals. Space-product development and assurance activities are aligned with the requirements of ISO 14300-1:2023 and ISO 14300-2:2023, together with the applicable ISO/ECSS technical standards identified through the project requirements and compliance matrix. Specific actuator verification and qualification tests under ECSS-Q-ST-60 / ECSS-E-ST-33 may be performed via established test houses and national facilities. 
NEMA Systems was formed following a decade of close working between NEMA UK Ltd, The University of Nottingham and Ultema Consultancy Ltd. It formalises the trusted relationship and allows NEMA Systems to benefit from the abilities and experience of all three founding parents of the business. Our team has a long history of developing and manufacturing actuators, motors and drives to create electro-mechanical systems for demanding environments. This experience informs the way we approach engineering, verification, manufacturing and programme delivery.

entityDescription:
Comobi – Orchestrating multimodal, autonomous-ready mobility
Ambition
Comobi BV (Gent, Belgium) runs a mobility platform for shared airport and station transfers. At its core is a proprietary pricing and matching algorithm. It groups passengers into shared rides, sets fair dynamic prices and assigns each trip to the right vehicle. Our ambition goes beyond one vehicle type or one fleet. We want to optimise the mobility system as a whole, planning across cars, vans, buses and, soon, autonomous shuttles as one coordinated network. This means fewer empty kilometres, higher occupancy and a lower cost and carbon footprint per passenger.
Why navigation and satellite technology matter in the shift to autonomy
Today a human driver fills the gaps in any mobility service. They read the traffic, handle a closed road, find the right terminal entrance and adjust when a flight lands early. Autonomous operations remove that human layer, so the intelligence has to move into the system itself.
In an autonomous model, Comobi acts as the service owner. It holds the customer demand, builds the trips and hands assignments to vehicle owners: autonomous operators running their own fleets. For this handover to work reliably, both sides need a shared, precise and constantly updated picture of the operating environment:
- High-integrity positioning and navigation (GNSS, including Galileo's high-accuracy and authentication services), so assignments, pick-up points and handovers are exact and trustworthy
- Satellite-based situational awareness, such as Earth observation, weather and real-time disruption data, so the service layer can re-plan routes, timing and vehicle allocation before problems reach the passenger
- Resilient connectivity, including satellite links where terrestrial networks fall short, so vehicles and the platform stay in contact at all times
Space-based data makes it possible to go from "dispatching a driver" to "orchestrating an autonomous fleet." It gives the service owner the context a human driver used to supply.
Multivendor collaboration
Comobi does not aim to build every component itself. We want to act as the neutral orchestration layer in a multivendor ecosystem. That means working with autonomous vehicle operators, navigation technology providers, satellite data providers and data storage and processing partners, with a preference for local and European partners. Our aim is to launch multivendor pilot operations. In these pilots, assignments, positioning data and situational information flow through open interfaces between the service owner and several vehicle operators. That makes autonomous mobility scalable, interoperable and grounded in European space capabilities.

description:
Zero Gravity Works is a European contract manufacturer of pharmaceutical crystals grown in low Earth orbit.
In microgravity the absence of gravity-driven convection lets crystals grow under diffusion-limited conditions, yielding a narrower and more uniform crystal size distribution than terrestrial processes reliably achieve at industrial scale. We crystallise a partner's small-molecule active pharmaceutical ingredient in orbit and deliver the drug substance back on Earth. For the partner it is a standard API supply relationship: the space complexity stays with us.
Two problems make this worth doing. A molecule can be stalled in development by its crystal form: a metastable polymorph that does not survive shelf life, or a commercial form whose quality varies from batch to batch in a narrow therapeutic index product. And a product approaching patent expiry can be defended with a new, patentable crystal form that a generic manufacturer cannot reproduce.
The system is a crystallisation module developed in four configurations: a ground unit that reproduces the process in the laboratory and establishes the reference data; a qualification unit for environmental and acceptance testing; a 12U CubeSat flight unit that crystallises in orbit and returns its measurements by telemetry; and a recovery module that brings material back to Earth. On-board process monitoring is based on Raman spectroscopy and microscopy.
Zero Gravity Works is participating in the ESA Business Incubation Centre Milan.
We are looking for partners and suppliers in CubeSat systems engineering and payload accommodation; ruggedisation and space qualification of optical instruments, in particular Raman spectrometers; thermal control and heat rejection for a liquid payload; launch and ground segment services; and solid-state analytical services for pharmaceutical materials.
entityDescription:
Zero Gravity Works (ZGW) is an Italian deep-tech company based in Milan, developing an orbital platform for the crystallisation of small-molecule pharmaceutical active ingredients.
In low Earth orbit, the absence of gravity-driven convection allows crystals to grow under diffusion-limited conditions, producing a narrower and more uniform size distribution than terrestrial processes reliably achieve at industrial scale. ZGW operates as a contract manufacturer of drug substance rather than as a drug developer: the molecule of a pharmaceutical partner is crystallised in orbit and the material is returned to Earth, while the space complexity remains with ZGW.
The system is built around a crystallisation module developed in successive configurations: a ground laboratory unit establishing the reference process, a qualification unit for environmental testing, a flight unit built to the 12U CubeSat standard returning its measurements by telemetry, and a recovery module returning the crystallised material in a re-entry capsule.
Core technical areas:
- macroscopic crystallisation reactor and fluidic handling for autonomous operation in microgravity
- in-situ Raman spectroscopy and optical microscopy, ruggedised for launch loads and the orbital environment
- thermal control, payload accommodation and mission and ground-segment design for a small satellite platform
- computational modelling of crystallisation dynamics in microgravity
Current activities focus on the preliminary design and feasibility of the orbital crystallisation module and on the feasibility and ruggedisation of the on-board Raman instrument, in collaboration with Politecnico di Milano and the University of Pavia. Technology Readiness Level: 3.
ZGW has been selected for incubation at ESA BIC Milan (2026–2028) and is registered as an innovative startup in the Italian Companies Register.

SENSE AI S.r.l. is an Italian innovative technology startup focused on the research, development and industrialisation of advanced Artificial Intelligence solutions, semantic data infrastructures and intelligent process automation.
The company develops a proprietary, scalable SaaS platform based on Large Language Models, multi-agent architectures, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic knowledge graphs, vector databases, predictive analytics and intelligent workflow automation. Its technological approach combines structured domain knowledge with generative AI, enabling the creation of specialised systems capable of processing complex information, supporting decision-making and automating highly regulated operational processes. 
SENSE AI adopts a model-agnostic architecture, integrating both commercial AI models through APIs and open-weight models deployed on dedicated GPU infrastructure. This approach reduces technological dependency on individual providers and allows sensitive information to be processed within controlled environments when required. The platform uses PostgreSQL with vector search capabilities, a proprietary knowledge graph and multi-agent RAG pipelines to retrieve, interpret and validate structured and unstructured information. 
A central element of the SENSE AI technology is its semantic knowledge infrastructure, designed to transform complex public and private datasets into interconnected, machine-readable knowledge. AI agents operate on this semantic layer to generate, classify, match and validate information, while automated validation mechanisms and mandatory human supervision ensure traceability, explainability and control over critical outputs. 
The technology is currently applied through two integrated vertical platforms, Sense Academy and Sense Worknet, dedicated respectively to digital learning, skills intelligence, workforce management and employment services. Both systems share the same semantic engine and knowledge infrastructure, creating a continuous data-driven connection between skills, training, professional profiles and operational requirements. 
SENSE AI's R&D activities include the development of knowledge graphs, generative AI systems, semantic matching engines, predictive models, explainable AI mechanisms, automated validation systems and specialised digital workflows. The company follows a human-in-the-loop approach in which AI supports professionals and operators without replacing human responsibility in critical decisions. 
The technological infrastructure is designed around security, scalability, interoperability and regulatory compliance. The architecture includes EU-based cloud infrastructure, granular role-based access control, immutable audit trails, secure data management and dedicated computing resources for AI workloads involving sensitive information. The company's development roadmap also includes compliance with GDPR and the EU AI Act, together with ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 certification pathways. 
SENSE AI's objective is to build specialised AI systems capable of transforming complex data, domain knowledge and operational rules into secure, explainable and scalable digital solutions.

The IMDEA Energy Institute is a research center created by the Regional Government of the Community of Madrid as a non-profit foundation to develop R&D activities, prioritizing scientific excellence, technology transfer, and social impact in the development of clean and renewable energy technologies in its objectives and daily work.
The IMDEA Energy Institute's main objective is to contribute to the development and establishment of a sustainable, fully decarbonized, economically competitive energy system that guarantees security of supply throughout the entire energy production, transformation, and end-use chain.
The IMDEA Energy Institute develops energy-related R&D activities by combining a policy of excellence in recruiting researchers, the implementation of appropriate scientific infrastructure, and the promotion of intense collaboration with the industrial sector. The quality of the research carried out by IMDEA Energy was recognized in 2020 with the prestigious accreditation as a "María de Maeztu" Research Unit awarded by the Ministry of Science and Innovation and in 2025 with th accreditation as a "Severo Ochoa" center.
R&D activities at IMDEA Energy are focused on seven main research themes:
- Production of sustainable fuels for effective decarbonization of the transport sector: hydrogen, biofuels, and other alternative fuels from renewable and/or residual sources.
- Solar energy systems and technologies, with a special emphasis on concentrated solar thermal energy for electricity production and industrial process heat.
- Energy storage using thermal, electrochemical, and thermochemical methods to increase the security of supply and penetration of renewable energy and distributed electricity generation.
- Smart management of electricity demand and improved reliability and stability of future power grids.
- Development of technologies and strategies for efficient end-use energy, with particular application to the development of a net-zero emissions industry.
- CCU routes for conversion into products of interest and high demand.
- Conducting sustainability studies on new energy technologies and systems and scenario modeling for energy planning.
The research objectives have been prioritized based on the main recommendations of the Scientific Council, as well as the challenges to be met in terms of decarbonization and circularity by 2030 and the future achievement of a carbon-neutral economy by 2050. These priorities have been complemented by the valorization and acceleration of the development of technological solutions for energy supply security, as promoted by the REPower Europe initiative to reduce energy dependence, and the preparation of strategies to anticipate the new challenges in industrial decarbonization envisaged in the Clean Industrial Deal.

ENT is a social economic initiative integrated by a multidisciplinary group of highly trained and experienced professionals dedicated to the elaboration, analysis and implementation of public environmental policies. Our activities are centred on the development of projects with a high component of innovation, with the desire to contribute to social change.
We focus on environmental taxation and economic instruments of environmental policy at international, national and local levels (environmentalization of tax ordinances or waste charges). We are experts in the evaluation of economic and environmental policies, through the use of applied economics methods, such as advanced statistical techniques, econometric modeling, input-output analysis, general equilibrium computable with environmental extensions, material flow accounting, etc.
We highlight our experience in economic aspects (costs and economic implications of waste policies) and in the design and evaluation of economic and fiscal policies (waste charges, pay-as-you-throw schemes, taxes on landfilling and incineration, deposit-refund schemes, fee-rebate systems, etc.).
We have also produced various waste management plans for local authorities. In particular, we have a lot of experience in the design and implementation of separate door to door collection schemes. Another priority area of work is waste food prevention.
